text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Panel (PT, PTT, Platelet Count)
The family history of joint swelling and bleeding suggests a possible clotting factor deficiency like Hemophilia. I need to check your clotting times to confirm.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Prothrombin Time: 15 sec, Partial Thromboplastin Time: 60 sec, Platelet Count: 160,000/mm3

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged PTT with normal PT and platelets points strongly toward Hemophilia A or B. Given the family history, I will order specific factor assays to distinguish between them. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and Factor IX Levels

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Factor VIII Level: 10% (Low), Factor IX Level: 95% (Normal)

speaker: Doctor
text: The low Factor VIII level confirms Hemophilia A. Do you recall any history of spontaneous joint bleeds, particularly in your knees or elbows, which is common in this condition?

speaker: Patient
